sentences.text: The skull of this pterosaur is toothless, relatively long, and features a straight, pointed beak with a large opening connecting the antorbital fenestra to the nostrils.
It had small eye sockets, lacked a lower jaw crest found in ornithocheiroids, but possessed a short projection at the back of the skull.
The estimated wingspan of the known individual is 1.7 meters.
The genus Jidapterus was named in 2003 by Dong Zhiming, Sun Yue-Wu, and Wu Shao-Yuan.
The type species of the genus is Jidapterus edentus.
The genus name combines "Jilin University" with the Greek word for wing.
The specific name edentus means "toothless" in Latin.
David Unwin initially placed Jidapterus in Tapejaridae but later agreed it belonged to the family Chaoyangopteridae as a close relative of Chaoyangopterus.
A 2017 redescription confirmed the placement of Jidapterus in Chaoyangopteridae and provided evidence distinguishing it from Chaoyangopterus.
The genus is classified within the family Chaoyangopteridae.
The Paleobiology Database lists Chaoyangopterinae as the parent group for Jidapterus.
The Paleobiology Database lists Tapejaridae as the family for Jidapterus.
Jidapterus lived during the Aptian stage of the Lower Cretaceous in the Jiufotang Formation of Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.
The classification of Jidapterus has been unstable, with original authors failing to assign it to a specific group.
There is a debate regarding whether Jidapterus is a basal azhdarchoid or closely related to Pteranodon and the genus Chaoyangopterus.
